title: Predicting Specialist Herbivore Distribution from Host Distribution Data
author: Brandon Fuller
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9gvh3w6
materials: For this exercise, specific software will need to downloaded. The first and most important software available is the statistical package called MaxEnt. You can find MaxEnt in the SDM Protocol folder in a Folder titled MaxEnt. This program should be ready to use and require no installation steps. You can read more about it here: https://biodiversityinformatics.amnh.org/open_source/maxent/ The MaxEnt program MaxEnt requires Java to run, so make sure you have the latest version installed: https://www.java.com/en/download/win10.jsp

Next, we will download the GIS software that will enable us to easily visualize the map. ArcGIS is one software that is widely used, but for the purposes of this guide, we will be using the free open-source program called QGIS. The download can be found at this link: https://qgis.org/en/site/forusers/download.html . At the download screen, download the long term release repository, which is QGIS version 3.10 at the time this was written. Download the "Long term release repository (most stable)" The link you choose will depend on what operating system you have, but make sure it is the long term stable release version. Once downloaded, install the program and follow the prompts in the setup launcher while choosing the default setup options.

steps.title: Initialize MaxEnt and Load Plant Data
steps.instruction: Open the MaxEnt software and import the host plant occurrence data.

substeps.instruction: Under the 'Samples' category, click browse and open 'Tsuga_canadensis_points.csv' from the GPS points folder.
Verify that a label with a checkbox called 'Tsuga_canadensis' is created.

steps.title: Import Bioclimatic Environmental Layers
steps.instruction: Load the raster data representing climatic factors into MaxEnt.

substeps.instruction: Under the 'Environmental layers' category, click browse.
Navigate to the raster data folder, ensure 'All Files' is selected as the file type, and open any of the bioclimatic files.
Confirm that all bioclimatic files are imported and that 'continuous' is selected next to each file name.

steps.title: Run Tsuga canadensis SDM
steps.instruction: Generate the Species Distribution Model (SDM) for the host plant.

substeps.instruction: Leave all options at default settings (specifically, do not check 'Create response curves' or 'Do jackknife to measure variable importance').
Click browse next to 'Output directory' and select the 'Tsuga canadensis model' folder under the 'Models' folder.
Click Run.
When the 'Outside bounding box' warning appears, click 'Suppress similar visual warnings'.
Wait for the process to complete (approximately 10+ minutes).

steps.title: Run Adelges tsugae Model Without Plant Data
steps.instruction: Create an insect distribution model using only bioclimatic data.

substeps.instruction: Under the 'Samples' category, click browse and open 'Adelges_tsugae_points.csv'.
Click browse next to 'Output directory' and select the 'Adelges tsugae model without plant data' folder within the 'Adelges tsugae models' folder.
Click Run and suppress any warnings.

steps.title: Prepare Plant SDM as Environmental Layer
steps.instruction: Integrate the previously generated plant model into the environmental data folder.

substeps.instruction: Locate the 'Tsuga_canadensis' ASC file in the 'Tsuga canadensis model' folder.
Copy and paste the 'Tsuga_canadensis' ASC file into the raster folder containing the bioclimatic layers.

steps.title: Run Adelges tsugae Model With Plant Data
steps.instruction: Create an insect distribution model that includes the host plant distribution as a predictor.

substeps.instruction: In MaxEnt, click browse under 'Environmental layers', ensure 'All Files' is selected, and open any bioclimatic file to refresh the list.
Verify that the host plant model is now listed at the bottom of the 'Environmental layers' category.
Change the 'Output directory' to the folder named 'Adelges tsugae model with plant data'.
Click Run.

steps.title: Visualize Models in QGIS
steps.instruction: Import and format the resulting ASC files in QGIS for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open QGIS and start a new project.
Locate and double-click the 'Tsuga_canadensis' ASC file to load the raster map.
Right-click the layer, select 'Properties', and navigate to the 'Symbology' tab.
Change the render type to 'Singleband pseudocolor'.
Select the 'spectral' color palette from the 'Color ramp' menu and click 'Invert Color Ramp'.
Click OK to save settings.

steps.title: Compare All Distribution Models
steps.instruction: Apply the same visualization settings to the insect models and compare results.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the symbology steps (Singleband pseudocolor, spectral palette, inverted ramp) for both Adelges tsugae models.
Rename the insect layers to 'with plants' and 'without plants' in the layer section to distinguish them.
Toggle visibility of the three maps to compare the distribution probabilities.
